newsitem.title: USA: U.S. trucking industry cheers choice to head DOT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. trucking industry cheers choice to head DOT.

text.p: The American Trucking Associations on Friday applauded President Clinton's choice of Rodney Slater, Administrator of the Federal Highway Administration, to be the new Transportation Secretary.

Thomas Donohue, president of the group, comprised of state trucking associations, said: "Rodney fully understands our nation's highway needs and that's critically important as we look forward to the reauthorization of America's core highway program in 1997.
"He knows transportation inside-out. He's a man of integrity. It's an outstanding choice."
However, consumer advocate Ralph Nader was critical of Slater's nomination.

"In his position as Federal Highway Administrator, Slater viewed the Department of Transportation largely as a financial service and consulting agency to transportation lobbies," Nader said in a statement.
"His operating procedure at FHWA is to ask the trucking industry and the highway lobby what they want and give it to them."
